```{r}
#this chunk creates the datasets from which complexity is measured, it takes the data and returns rows = classes (distinct exponent combinations) and lexeme counts for each class
#these are the functions used across the dialect datasets
#starting with a "full" data, including all small classes

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(rlang)
library(ggplot2)

#for the full datasets based on MN_class data
combine_lexeme_values_full <- function(data) {
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(
      MN_class = ifelse(Cell == "inf", "non", MN_class)
    )
  # Combine lexeme values and summarize
  combined_values_full <- data %>%
    group_by(Lexeme) %>%
    summarise(
      infinitive = first(MN_class[Cell == "inf"]),
      present    = first(MN_class[Cell == "pres"]),
      preterite  = first(MN_class[Cell == "pret"]),
      supine     = first(MN_class[Cell == "sup"]),
      .groups = 'drop'  # Drop grouping after summarizing
    )
  
   # One row per class, with lexeme_count and class_weight = 1
   total_lexeme_counts_full <- combined_values_full %>%
    group_by(infinitive, present, preterite, supine) %>%
    summarise(
      lexeme_count = n(),      # number of lexemes with this pattern
      class_weight = 1,        # one class per row
      .groups      = "drop"
    )
  
  total_lexeme_counts_full
}

#for the hypothetical datasets

combine_lexeme_values_hist_status <- function(data) {
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(
      Hist_status = ifelse(Cell == "inf", "non", Hist_status),
    )
  
  combined_values_hist_status <- data %>%
    group_by(Lexeme) %>%
    summarise(
      infinitive = first(Hist_status[Cell == "inf"]),
      present    = first(Hist_status[Cell == "pres"]),
      preterite  = first(Hist_status[Cell == "pret"]),
      supine     = first(Hist_status[Cell == "sup"]),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )

  # One row per pattern (class), with lexeme_count and class_weight = 1
  total_lexeme_counts_hist_status <- combined_values_hist_status %>%
    group_by(infinitive, present, preterite, supine) %>%
    summarise(
      lexeme_count = n(),      # number of lexemes with this pattern
      class_weight = 1,        # one class per pattern row
      .groups      = "drop"
    )
  
  total_lexeme_counts_hist_status
}
```


```{r}
#this is the first entropy measurement. This reflects "full" competence, the knowledge of which cells for which classes/lexemes are overabundant. It takes overabundant exponents "a/e" as exponents in their own right

# General function to calculate conditional entropy for any two paradigm members
calculate_conditional_entropy <- function(data,
                                          condition_col, #the cell from which we are "guessing"
                                          target_col, #the cell to which we are guessing
                                          weighted = FALSE) {
  
  condition_str <- as.character(condition_col)
  target_str    <- as.character(target_col)
  
  # Choose which weight to use:
  # - weighted = FALSE -> class_weight  (class-based)
  # - weighted = TRUE  -> lexeme_count  (lexeme-based)
  weight_col <- if (weighted) "lexeme_count" else "class_weight"
  
  #figure out the total number of rows(=classes) or lexemes within the dataframe
  total_mass <- sum(data[[weight_col]])
  
  # This will store H(target | condition)
  conditional_entropy_total <- 0
  
  # We want to get all distinct condition values (e.g., a, a/e and e within present)
  condition_values <- unique(data[[condition_str]])
  
  #now we want to iterate over them
  for (condition_value in condition_values) {
    rows_with_condition <- data[data[[condition_str]] == condition_value, ]
    if (nrow(rows_with_condition) == 0) next
    
    # 1b. compute P(condition = condition_value)
    mass_for_condition <- sum(rows_with_condition[[weight_col]])
    p_condition <- mass_for_condition / total_mass
    if (p_condition == 0) next
    
    # 1c. compute distribution of target values given this condition value
    target_mass_by_value <- tapply(
      rows_with_condition[[weight_col]],
      rows_with_condition[[target_str]],
      sum
    )
    
    target_mass_by_value <- target_mass_by_value[target_mass_by_value > 0]
    if (length(target_mass_by_value) == 0) next
    
    # P(target = value | condition = condition_value)
    target_probabilities <- as.numeric(target_mass_by_value) /
                            sum(target_mass_by_value)
    
    # 1d. entropy for this condition value: H(target | condition = value)
    entropy_given_condition <- -sum(
      target_probabilities * log2(target_probabilities)
    )
    
    
    # 1e. add contribution to the total entropy: P(condition) * H(target | condition)
    conditional_entropy_total <- conditional_entropy_total +
      p_condition * entropy_given_condition
  }
  
  
  # STEP 2: H(target | condition)
  return(conditional_entropy_total)
}


# Function to calculate average conditional entropies for cell combinations, takes the function above
average_conditional_entropy <- function(data) {
  
  cells <- c("infinitive", "present", "preterite", "supine")
  
  # All ordered pairs (condition, target), condition != target
  pairs <- expand.grid(
    condition = cells,
    target    = cells,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  pairs <- subset(pairs, condition != target)
  
  # For each pair, compute H(target | condition), unweighted and weighted
  H_unw <- mapply(function(cond, targ) {
    calculate_conditional_entropy(
      data          = data,
      condition_col = cond,
      target_col    = targ,
      weighted      = FALSE
    )
  }, cond = pairs$condition, targ = pairs$target)
  
  H_w <- mapply(function(cond, targ) {
    calculate_conditional_entropy(
      data          = data,
      condition_col = cond,
      target_col    = targ,
      weighted      = TRUE
    )
  }, cond = pairs$condition, targ = pairs$target)
  
  list(
    pairs    = pairs,
    H_unw    = H_unw,
    H_w      = H_w,
    avg_unw  = mean(H_unw),
    avg_w    = mean(H_w)
  )
}

global_entropy <- function(data,
                           cells = c("infinitive", "present", "preterite", "supine"),
                           weighted = FALSE) {
  # Use existing function
  res <- average_conditional_entropy(data)
  
  if (weighted) {
    res$avg_w   # lexeme-weighted mean entropy
  } else {
    res$avg_unw # class-based mean entropy
  }
}

```

```{r}
#this chunk is to create datasets where overabundant cells are redistributed, so overabundance is not taken as an exponent in its own right
#after splitting, the same entropy function as above can be applied further
#this is based on Helens code


split_overabundant_cells <- function(df) {

  
  weight_cols <- c("class_weight", "lexeme_count")
  # only keep weight columns that are actually present
  weight_cols <- intersect(weight_cols, names(df))
  
  # all other columns are potential places for "a/e" etc.
  cols_to_check <- setdiff(colnames(df), weight_cols)
  
  changed <- TRUE
  while (changed) {
    changed <- FALSE
    new_rows <- list()
    new_row_index <- 1
    
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
      row <- df[i, , drop = FALSE]
      split_done <- FALSE
      
      for (col in cols_to_check) {
        val <- row[[col]]
        
        if (is.character(val) && grepl("/", val, fixed = TRUE)) {
          parts   <- strsplit(val, "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
          n_parts <- length(parts)
          
          for (p in parts) {
            new_row <- row
            new_row[[col]] <- p
            
            # divide all weight columns equally
            for (wcol in weight_cols) {
              new_row[[wcol]] <- row[[wcol]] / n_parts
            }
            
            new_rows[[new_row_index]] <- new_row
            new_row_index <- new_row_index + 1
          }
          
          split_done <- TRUE
          changed <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }
      
      if (!split_done) {
        new_rows[[new_row_index]] <- row
        new_row_index <- new_row_index + 1
      }
    }
    
    df <- do.call(rbind, new_rows)
    rownames(df) <- NULL
  }
  
  df
}


```


```{r}

#functions related to the probability of success/accuracy measure

#first we want to expand any sources that are overabundant, so that guessing from an overabundant source a/e is like guessing from a and guessing from e. Both of these will get a weight of 0.5, so that the total weight of that row remains the same.

#we want to keep overabundant targets, because those give us two correct guesses

#same logic as above, but spliting only condition, not targets

split_overabundant_condition <- function(df, condition_col) {
  condition_str <- as.character(condition_col)
  
  # we assume df already has class_weight and lexeme_count
  weight_cols <- intersect(c("class_weight", "lexeme_count"), names(df))
  
  if (!condition_str %in% names(df)) {
    stop("Column '", condition_str, "' not found in data.")
  }
  
  changed <- TRUE
  while (changed) {
    changed <- FALSE
    new_rows <- list()
    new_row_index <- 1
    
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
      row <- df[i, , drop = FALSE]
      val <- row[[condition_str]]
      
      if (is.character(val) && grepl("/", val, fixed = TRUE)) {
        parts   <- strsplit(val, "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
        n_parts <- length(parts)
        
        for (p in parts) {
          new_row <- row
          new_row[[condition_str]] <- p
          
          # divide all weight columns equally
          for (wcol in weight_cols) {
            new_row[[wcol]] <- row[[wcol]] / n_parts
          }
          
          new_rows[[new_row_index]] <- new_row
          new_row_index <- new_row_index + 1
        }
        
        changed <- TRUE
      } else {
        new_rows[[new_row_index]] <- row
        new_row_index <- new_row_index + 1
      }
    }
    
    df <- do.call(rbind, new_rows)
    rownames(df) <- NULL
  }
  
  df
}

#here we want to access the probabilities of targets within each source. So for example, if we have source a, and the possible targets are a, e and a/e, we want to know what the probabilities of those targets are. The overabundant targets a/e contribute 0.5 to each target (this is just for probabilities of targets) // the weight of the target also depends on the weight of the pattern (after splitting some patterns get .05)

compute_probs_by_condition <- function(data_with_weight,
                                       condition_str,
                                       target_str) {
  # data_with_weight must have column 'weight'
  
  data_with_weight %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[condition_str]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      w_a = sum(
        dplyr::case_when(
          .data[[target_str]] == "a"   ~ weight,
          .data[[target_str]] == "a/e" ~ 0.5 * weight,
          TRUE                         ~ 0
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      w_e = sum(
        dplyr::case_when(
          .data[[target_str]] == "e"   ~ weight,
          .data[[target_str]] == "a/e" ~ 0.5 * weight,
          TRUE                         ~ 0
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      w_non = sum(
        dplyr::case_when(
          .data[[target_str]] == "non" ~ weight,
          TRUE                         ~ 0
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      total_w_cat = w_a + w_e + w_non,
      P_a   = ifelse(total_w_cat > 0, w_a   / total_w_cat, NA_real_),
      P_e   = ifelse(total_w_cat > 0, w_e   / total_w_cat, NA_real_),
      P_non = ifelse(total_w_cat > 0, w_non / total_w_cat, NA_real_)
    )
}


#here we want to compute the probability of success. Here the overabundant targets such as a/e will have two correct targets, that is both a and e are correct. The other will only have one correct target. Probability of success is the probability of correct target or targets in the case of overabundance (so a sum). For overabundant lexemes, this will add up to 1, because both choices will be correct.
attach_best_guess_accuracy <- function(data_with_weight,
                                       probs_by_condition,
                                       condition_str,
                                       target_str) {
  data_with_weight %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      probs_by_condition,
      by = setNames(condition_str, condition_str)
    ) %>%
    # choose best guess per row
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      best_guess = {
        # vector of probs in a fixed order
        probs <- c(P_a, P_e, P_non)
        names(probs) <- c("a", "e", "non")
        # index of max (first max if tie)
        if (all(is.na(probs))) {
          NA_character_
        } else {
          names(probs)[which.max(probs)]
        }
      }
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    # correctness of best guess for this row
    dplyr::mutate(
      correct = dplyr::case_when(
        # simple targets
        .data[[target_str]] == "a"   & best_guess == "a"   ~ 1,
        .data[[target_str]] == "e"   & best_guess == "e"   ~ 1,
        .data[[target_str]] == "non" & best_guess == "non" ~ 1,
        # overabundant target: a/e → correct if best_guess is a or e
        .data[[target_str]] == "a/e" & best_guess %in% c("a", "e") ~ 1,
        TRUE ~ 0
      )
    )
}

#here we want to compute the accuracy for the entire source. So say, we have the source a, and now we know probability of success for each pattern within this source. We want now to weight those probabilities against the weight of that pattern and then sum them

summarise_accuracy_by_condition <- function(data_with_correct,
                                            condition_str) {
  data_with_correct %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[condition_str]]) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      total_weight = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      row_share    = dplyr::if_else(
        total_weight > 0,
        weight / total_weight,
        NA_real_
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      total_weight = dplyr::first(total_weight),
      accuracy = dplyr::if_else(
        total_weight > 0,
        sum(row_share * correct, na.rm = TRUE),
        NA_real_
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

#finally we want to compute accuracy for one pair of cells. That is in most cases, one pair of cells will have more than one source, and for each of these sources we have computed accuracy. Now we want to compute the total accuracy, which will be weighting the accuracies of the the sources against the total weight and summing that up

accuracy_one_pair <- function(data,
                              condition_col,
                              target_col,
                              weighted = FALSE) {
  condition_str <- as.character(condition_col)
  target_str    <- as.character(target_col)
  
  # data must already have class_weight and lexeme_count
  weight_col <- if (weighted) "lexeme_count" else "class_weight"
  
  data_local <- data
  data_local$weight <- data_local[[weight_col]]
  
  # 1. expand overabundance only in the condition column
  data_expanded <- split_overabundant_condition(
    df            = data_local,
    condition_col = condition_str
  )
  
  # after splitting, reset generic weight from the chosen column
  data_expanded$weight <- data_expanded[[weight_col]]
  
  # 2. get P_a, P_e, P_non per condition value
  probs_by_condition <- compute_probs_by_condition(
    data_with_weight = data_expanded,
    condition_str    = condition_str,
    target_str       = target_str
  )
  
  # 3. attach best_guess and row-wise correctness
  data_with_correct <- attach_best_guess_accuracy(
    data_with_weight  = data_expanded,
    probs_by_condition = probs_by_condition,
    condition_str      = condition_str,
    target_str         = target_str
  )
  
  # 4. per-condition accuracy
  accuracies_by_condition <- summarise_accuracy_by_condition(
    data_with_correct,
    condition_str
  ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(condition_value = !!condition_str) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      condition_col = condition_str,
      target_col    = target_str
    )
  
  # sanity check: accuracies in [0,1]
  bad <- accuracies_by_condition %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(accuracy) & (accuracy < -1e-8 | accuracy > 1 + 1e-8))
  if (nrow(bad) > 0) {
    stop("Accuracy out of [0,1] for some condition values:\n",
         paste(utils::capture.output(print(bad)), collapse = "\n"))
  }
  
  # 5. pair-level accuracy (weighted average of per-condition accuracies)
  by_condition2 <- accuracies_by_condition %>%
    dplyr::rename(condition_weight = total_weight)
  
  pair_acc <- by_condition2 %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      pair_total_weight = sum(condition_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      condition_share   = dplyr::if_else(
        pair_total_weight > 0,
        condition_weight / pair_total_weight,
        NA_real_
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      pair_total_weight = dplyr::first(pair_total_weight),
      accuracy = dplyr::if_else(
        pair_total_weight > 0,
        sum(condition_share * accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
        NA_real_
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      condition_col = condition_str,
      target_col    = target_str
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(condition_col, target_col, pair_total_weight, accuracy)
  
  # sanity check pair-level
  bad_pair <- pair_acc %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(accuracy) & (accuracy < -1e-8 | accuracy > 1 + 1e-8))
  if (nrow(bad_pair) > 0) {
    stop("Pair accuracy out of [0,1] for pair:\n",
         paste(utils::capture.output(print(bad_pair)), collapse = "\n"))
  }
  
  list(
    pair_accuracy          = pair_acc,
    accuracies_by_condition = accuracies_by_condition
  )
}

#accuracy of all pairs:
accuracy_all_pairs <- function(data, cells, weighted = FALSE) {
  pairs <- expand.grid(
    condition_col = cells,
    target_col    = cells,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(condition_col != target_col)
  
  res_list <- purrr::map(
    seq_len(nrow(pairs)),
    ~ {
      cc <- pairs$condition_col[.x]
      tc <- pairs$target_col[.x]
      accuracy_one_pair(data, cc, tc, weighted = weighted)
    }
  )
  
  pair_acc    <- purrr::map_dfr(res_list, "pair_accuracy")
  by_condition <- purrr::map_dfr(res_list, "accuracies_by_condition")
  
  bad_pairs <- pair_acc %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(accuracy) & (accuracy < -1e-8 | accuracy > 1 + 1e-8))
  if (nrow(bad_pairs) > 0) {
    stop("Pair accuracy out of [0,1] for some pairs:\n",
         paste(utils::capture.output(print(bad_pairs)), collapse = "\n"))
  }
  
  list(
    pair_accuracy          = pair_acc,
    accuracies_by_condition = by_condition
  )
}

global_accuracy <- function(pair_accuracy) {
  pair_accuracy %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      accuracy = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups  = "drop"
    )
}

global_accuracy_best_guess <- function(data,
                                       cells = c("infinitive", "present", "preterite", "supine"),
                                       weighted = FALSE) {
  # compute accuracy for all ordered cell pairs
  res_pairs <- accuracy_all_pairs(
    data     = data,
    cells    = cells,
    weighted = weighted
  )
  
  # res_pairs$pair_accuracy must have a column 'accuracy'
  # global_accuracy(...) returns a 1-row data frame with column 'accuracy'
  global_accuracy(res_pairs$pair_accuracy)$accuracy
}

global_accuracy_both <- function(data,
                                 cells = c("infinitive", "present", "preterite", "supine")) {
  acc_unw <- global_accuracy_best_guess(data, cells, weighted = FALSE)
  acc_w   <- global_accuracy_best_guess(data, cells, weighted = TRUE)
  
  list(
    class_based  = acc_unw,
    lexeme_based = acc_w
  )
}

```



#here I run functions separately for each dialect, because i wanted to be able to see numbers for each dialect. This is of course possible to simplify and have a function which takes each dataset one by one and returns the result

```{r}
#Strand


folder_path <- "datasets/G_lists_dataset"

file_path_Strand <- file.path(folder_path, "Strand.csv")

Strand_data <- read.csv(
  file_path_Strand,
  sep = ";",
  header = TRUE
)

lexemes_Strand <- Strand_data %>%
  filter(Hist_status %in% c("a", "e")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Class_label) & Class_label != "") %>%
  pull(Lexeme) %>%
  unique() 

filtered_data_Strand <- Strand_data %>%
  filter(Lexeme %in% lexemes_Strand)


#datasets
df_full_Strand <- combine_lexeme_values_full(filtered_data_Strand)

df_ov_Strand <- split_overabundant_cells(df_full_Strand)

df_hyp_Strand <- combine_lexeme_values_hist_status(filtered_data_Strand)




```

```{r}
  ),
  
  full = list(
    df_full_Avaldsnes,
    df_full_Fitjar, df_full_Herdla, df_full_Meland, df_full_Odda, df_full_Sjernaroey, df_full_Sogndal, df_full_Strand, df_full_Suldal, df_full_Ulvik, df_full_Lavik, df_full_Nordfjord, df_full_Syvde
  ),
  
  ov = list(
    df_ov_Avaldsnes,
    df_ov_Fitjar, df_ov_Herdla, df_ov_Meland, df_ov_Odda, df_ov_Sjernaroey, df_ov_Sogndal, df_ov_Strand, df_ov_Suldal, df_ov_Ulvik, df_ov_Lavik, df_ov_Nordfjord, df_ov_Syvde
  ),
  
  hyp = list(
    df_hyp_Avaldsnes,
    df_hyp_Fitjar, df_hyp_Herdla, df_hyp_Meland, df_hyp_Odda, df_hyp_Sjernaroey, df_hyp_Sogndal, df_hyp_Strand, df_hyp_Suldal, df_hyp_Ulvik, df_hyp_Lavik, df_hyp_Nordfjord, df_hyp_Syvde
```

```{r}
#take dataset, return table for the measures

cells <- c("infinitive", "present", "preterite", "supine")

measure_entropy_one <- function(data, label) {
  tibble::tibble(
    system_label = label,
    measure      = "entropy",
    weighting    = c("class", "lexeme"),
    value        = c(
      global_entropy(data, cells, weighted = FALSE),
      global_entropy(data, cells, weighted = TRUE)
    )
  )
}

measure_accuracy_one <- function(data, label) {
  tibble::tibble(
    system_label = label,
    measure      = "best_guess_accuracy",
    weighting    = c("class", "lexeme"),
    value        = c(
      global_accuracy_best_guess(data, cells, weighted = FALSE),
      global_accuracy_best_guess(data, cells, weighted = TRUE)
    )
  )
}


```

```{r}
#run all together

results_all <- systems_all %>%
  dplyr::rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    measures = list(dplyr::bind_rows(
      # entropy for all 3
      measure_entropy_one(full, "full_attested"),
      measure_entropy_one(ov,   "ov_attested"),
      measure_entropy_one(hyp,  "hypothetical"),
      
      # accuracy only for full and hypothetical
      measure_accuracy_one(full, "full_attested"),
      measure_accuracy_one(hyp,  "hypothetical")
    ))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::unnest(measures)

results_diff <- results_all %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = c(dialect, measure, weighting),
    names_from  = system_label,
    values_from = value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    diff_full_minus_hyp = full_attested - hypothetical,
    diff_ov_minus_hyp   = ov_attested   - hypothetical
  )

#means and sd across the different results
mean_SD <- results_all %>%
  group_by(system_label, measure, weighting) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_value   = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


```

```{r}
#plotting

dialect_order <- c(
  "Strand", "Sjernaroey", "Avaldsnes", "Fitjar", "Herdla", "Meland", "Sogndal", "Suldal", "Odda",  "Ulvik",
  "Lavik", "Nordfjord", "Syvde"
)

results_all  <- results_all  %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dialect = factor(dialect, levels = dialect_order))

results_diff <- results_diff %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dialect = factor(dialect, levels = dialect_order))

entropy_diff <- results_diff %>%
  dplyr::filter(measure == "entropy")

p_full <- ggplot(entropy_diff,
       aes(x = dialect,
           y = diff_full_minus_hyp,
           fill = weighting)) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    width    = 0.6,
    colour   = "black",
    size     = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(diff_full_minus_hyp, 2)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    vjust    = -0.3,    
    colour   = "black",
    size     = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
  name   = "Weighting scheme",
  values = c(
    "class"  = "#BDBDBD",
    "lexeme" = "#0072B2"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "class"  = "By class",
    "lexeme" = "By lexeme"
  )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Dialect point",
    y = "Difference in average \n conditional entropy in bits \n (attested  − hypothetical)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 14
    ),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggsave("entropy_diff.png", p_full,
       width  = 9,  
       height = 5,
       units  = "in",
       dpi    = 300)


p_distr <- ggplot(entropy_diff,
       aes(x = dialect,
           y = diff_ov_minus_hyp,
           fill = weighting)) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    width    = 0.6,
    colour   = "black",
    size     = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(diff_ov_minus_hyp, 2)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    vjust    = -0.3,    
    colour   = "black",
    size     = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
  name   = "Weighting scheme",
  values = c(
    "class"  = "#BDBDBD",
    "lexeme" = "#0072B2"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "class"  = "By class",
    "lexeme" = "By lexeme"
  )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Dialect point",
    y = "Difference in average \n conditional entropy in bits \n (attested  − hypothetical)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 14
    ),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggsave("entropy_diff_distrib.png", p_distr,
       width  = 9,  
       height = 5,
       units  = "in",
       dpi    = 300)


acc_scatter <- results_diff %>%
  dplyr::filter(measure == "best_guess_accuracy")


p_acc <- ggplot(acc_scatter,
       aes(x = dialect,
           y = diff_full_minus_hyp,
           fill = weighting)) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    width    = 0.6,
    colour   = "black",
    size     = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(diff_full_minus_hyp, 2),
      y     = diff_full_minus_hyp + ifelse(diff_full_minus_hyp >= 0, 0.01, -0.01)
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    vjust    = 0.5,
    colour   = "black",
    size     = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
  name   = "Weighting scheme",
  values = c(
    "class"  = "#BDBDBD",
    "lexeme" = "#0072B2"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "class"  = "By class",
    "lexeme" = "By lexeme"
  )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Dialect point",
    y = "Difference in average \n probability of success \n(attested − hypothetical)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 14
    ),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggsave("acc_distrib.png", p_acc,
       width  = 9,  
       height = 5,
       units  = "in",
       dpi    = 300)
```
